sections.heading: When to use
sections.text: For flyback converters, start with current-mode control. For low-power (<75W) isolated applications, the flyback is the default choice. Primary-side regulation (PSR) eliminates the optocoupler but limits transient response. Secondary-side feedback with optocoupler gives better regulation.

sections.heading: Design formulas
sections.text: Turns ratio N = Np/Ns. CCM: Vout = Vin*D/(N*(1-D)). DCM: Vout = Vin*D*sqrt(R_load/(2*L_mag*fsw))/N. RHPZ in CCM: f_RHPZ = R_load*(1-D)^2/(2*pi*L_mag*D). Slope compensation: m_c >= (Vout*N+Vin)/(2*L_mag*fsw).

sections.heading: CCM/DCM transition
sections.text: The CCM/DCM boundary occurs at I_load_boundary = (Vin-Vout*D)*D/(2*L_mag*fsw*N). Below this load, the plant changes from double-pole+RHPZ to single-pole. Design compensation for worst case (CCM at full load) and accept larger margins in DCM.

sections.heading: Constraint
sections.text: Leading-edge blanking on the current sense signal is mandatory for flyback to filter the leakage inductance spike at turn-on. Typical blanking time: 100-300ns depending on leakage. If the design spans CCM and DCM, document the intended operating region.

sections.heading: Escalation trigger
sections.text: If flyback with PSR fails transient specs, escalate to secondary-side feedback with optocoupler. If current-mode still fails, the flyback topology itself may be the limit — consider forward or half-bridge for higher power.
